text.p: Hein-Werner Corp, the leading worldwide manufacturer and marketer of collision repair equipment, said Friday it was looking at a range of potential strategic and smaller product line acquisitions.

"Our intent is to use the cash from our recent divestitures to expand into markets which are counter-cyclical to the automotive industry," Joseph Dindorf, president, said in a statement. "This will provide the company with the ability to maintain long-term stability and growth over the course of future business cycles and fluctuating economic conditions."

In May, Hein-Werner completed the sale of Great Bend Industries, its fluid power business, for $22.5 million in cash. In June, it signed a letter of intent to sell Winona Van Norman, its engine rebuilding division. That deal is expected to close in August.
"When these transactions are completed, we expect to have over $3.00 per share in cash, net of related income tax, to invest in the business," Dindorf said.
He added that the core collision repair business is having another good year, following a record year in 1996.

North American sales and earnings for the second quarter were up. International sales for the second quarter and first half were down slightly from 1996 due to weak business conditions in most of Western Europe, particularly France.

"We expect to absorb some costs for the rest of the year associated with the first quarter consolidation of certain European sales facilities," Dindorf said. "Sales in eastern Europe and the Far East are strong, and we expect this trend to continue for the balance of the year."
